table.loading: Please wait while we retrieve the area soils...
table.textureTooltip: Soil texture refers to the mix of different particle sizes in soil. There are 13 texture classes (USDA): Clay (heavy), Silty clay, Clay (light), Silty clay loam, Clay loam, Silt, Silt loam, Sandy clay, Loam, Sandy clay loam, Sandy loam, Loamy sand, Sand.
table.drainageTooltip: Drainage class describes how often and how long soil stays wet. Classes: E (Excessively), SE (Somewhat excessively), W (Well), MW (Moderately well), I (Imperfectly), P (Poorly), VP (Very poorly) drained.
table.colourTooltip: Soil colour is influenced by organic matter, minerals, and moisture. Described as: Blackish, Blueish/greenish/grayish, Brownish, Reddish, Whitish, Yellowish.
table.coarseTooltip: Coarse fragments are solid particles > 2mm (gravel, cobbles, stones). They affect water retention, drainage, and root penetration.
table.mottleTooltip: Mottles are spots of different colours within the dominant soil colour, indicating alternating wet and dry conditions.
table.wrbTooltip: WRB soil classification codes: AC=Acrisols, AL=Alisols, AN=Andosols, AR=Arenosols, AT=Anthrosols, CH=Chernozems, CL=Calcisols, CM=Cambisols, FL=Fluvisols, FR=Ferralsols, GL=Gleysols, GY=Gypsisols, HS=Histosols, KS=Kastanozems, LP=Leptosols, LV=Luvisols, LX=Lixisols, NT=Nitisols, PH=Phaeozems, PL=Planosols, PT=Plinthosols, PZ=Podzols, RG=Regosols, RT=Retisols, SC=Solonchaks, SN=Solonetz, ST=Stagnosols, TC=Technosols, UM=Umbrisols, VR=Vertisols.
table.shareTooltip: Share at location refers to the percentage of soil present within the soil mapping unit at the selected location.

questionnaire.intro: Click on the buttons below to start recalculating your soil
questionnaire.topsoilNote: This evaluation will focus on the topsoil in our area which represents the upper 0 - 20 cm of the soil layer.

texture.title: Soil texture test
texture.ballTest: Ball Test: Can you make a ball with the soil when it's moist?
texture.ballDesc: Assess soil cohesiveness by forming a ball and observing if it holds or crumbles.
texture.ribbonTest: Ribbon Test: Can you make a ribbon by pressing the soil between your thumb and finger?
texture.ribbonDesc: Form a ribbon with soil and measure its length before breaking to assess texture.
texture.ribbonLength: Ribbon Length: How long is the ribbon you can make?
texture.ribbonLengthDesc: Measure ribbon length to estimate clay content in soil.
texture.grittiness: Grittiness: Does the soil feel gritty?
texture.grittinessDesc: Feel for gritty particles in moistened soil to determine sand content.
texture.smoothness: Smoothness: How smooth is the soil?
texture.smoothnessDesc: Assess silt content by evaluating how smooth the soil feels when rubbed.
texture.stickiness: Stickiness: How sticky is the soil?
texture.stickinessDesc: Test how sticky the soil feels to estimate clay content.

drainage.title: Drainage test
drainage.instruction: Select one of the characteristics below
drainage.excessive: Excessively Drained: Water moves through your soil very quickly
drainage.somewhatExcessive: Somewhat Excessively Drained: Water moves quickly through your soil, but not as fast as excessively drained soils
drainage.well: Well Drained: Water moves through your soil at a balanced speed, keeping it from being too wet or too dry.
drainage.moderatelyWell: Moderately Well Drained: Your soil drains slower, but it doesn't stay wet for a long time
drainage.imperfect: Imperfectly Drained: Water drains slowly, sometimes causing wet spots in your soil
drainage.poor: Poorly Drained: Does water drain very slowly, leaving the soil waterlogged?

constraints.title: CONSTRAINTS AFFECTING YOUR CROP YIELD
constraints.subtitle: Constraints for
constraints.thermalTooltip: Thermal constraint measures how temperature conditions limit crop growth and yield at this location. It reflects the extent to which factors such as extreme temperatures, short growing seasons, and heat stress during sensitive growth stages may reduce crop productivity.
constraints.moistureTooltip: Moisture constraint measures the impact of soil moisture availability on crop yield potential. It reflects how factors such as rainfall availability, drought conditions, evapotranspiration, and seasonal water balance may limit crop productivity.
constraints.explanation: These indicators show how strongly local climate conditions may limit crop growth and yield:
constraints.lowerValuesDesc: → fewer climate limitations and better suitability for the crop.
constraints.higherValuesDesc: → stronger climate limitations and lower suitability.
constraints.sourceLink: Crop yield constraint factor - GAEZ v5
